answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can earn reputation or claim work. A grove of new accounts may appear instantly, but each must tie up capital, and cheating risks forfeiting the deposit when a challenge exposes duplicate control or fabricated work. The cost scales with the number of identities: an attacker needs more capital and bears more risk to collect nectar across the dune of otherwise cheap accounts.
